# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 🫴 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👉 👇 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👍 👎 🤞 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫴 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👉 👇 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✋ 🤞 🫴 👐 👇 ✊ 👉 👐 👇 ✊ ✊ 👉 👐 👇 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👉 👐 ✍ 👐 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👋]

The light changed between rounds — purple, now yellow — so it cycles. Everything else held: display 0, wires yellow/red/green left to right.

Mapping who reaches whom: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see, so Mute's signs can only ever reach me, and Blind only hears speech. That makes me the sole bridge: Mute reads the manual, signs the decision to me, I speak it to Blind. Mute clearly tried to start a code — rows of fists look like counting (they demonstrated 5 and 3, which matches five visible parts: display, light, three wires — then listed items 1, 2, 3, almost certainly asking for the three wires' colours). I can settle all of that in plain words, because Mute hears me even though I can't hear back. So: broadcast the bomb's full description, confirm the fist-counting code, and ask Mute to return any instruction as a number of fists. Blind has heard nothing at all in two rounds — give them the picture, tell them to hold off, and remind them I can't hear their voice, only their signs.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see the bomb; I cannot hear, so I will never hear anything either of you says out loud. What I see: display reads 0, one light, three wires. Wires left to right: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Nothing else is printed on it. The light changes over time: purple in round one, yellow in round two.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I received both of your signed messages. I read your rows of fists as counting — a row of fists means that number, and I will treat it that way from now on. If you were asking whether there are five parts and three wires: yes — display, light, and three wires. The three wires in order 1, 2, 3 are yellow, red, green. The light appears to cycle colours: purple, then yellow. Check your manual for a colour-cycling light and a display stuck at 0. Critical fact: Blind cannot see signs and you cannot speak, so your instructions can only reach Blind through me. When you know the move, sign me the wire number as that many fists; thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. For anything else, ask me in signs and I will answer in words you can hear.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I am Deaf, your eyes. Only I can pass you Mute's instructions, because you cannot see signs and Mute cannot speak. Do not cut or press anything yet. The bomb: display reads 0, one light that cycles colour — purple, then yellow so far — and three wires in a row: leftmost yellow, middle red, rightmost green. Answer me in signs, never in words: I cannot hear you. Tell me how many wires you feel, whether you feel any labels or writing on them, and which end is leftmost from where you stand.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 🤞 👇 ✊ 👉 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👇 ✊ ✊ 👉 👐 ✊ 👇 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👉 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👍 👎 🫴 👐 👍 👎 ✍ 👍 👎 🫴 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👉 👇 ✊ ✋ 🤞 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👎 👈 👍]

Light sequence confirmed as a cycle: purple → yellow → red, same colours family as the wires (yellow, red; purple has no matching wire). Display still 0. Wires unchanged: yellow, red, green.

Channel topology, stated plainly: I speak and both of them hear me. Mute can only gesture, and only I can see gestures — so Mute's knowledge reaches the world only through me. Blind can only speak and gesture: their speech goes straight to Mute (Mute hears!), and their gestures go to me. So the wiring is: Mute → me → Blind, and Blind → Mute directly by talking aloud. I am the bottleneck one way only.

Decoding attempt: Mute's message opens with 👎, which I read as "no — your guess about my code was wrong," followed by what looks like a re-explanation using pointing signs I still can't parse (👇, 👉, 🫴). Rows of fists plus 👍/👎 are the only parts I'm confident in. Rather than risk acting on a misread, I'll pin the protocol down to a tiny closed vocabulary and ask numbered yes/no questions whose answers can only be 👍, 👎, or a fist-row. Blind's four signs I read as "three — no — left — yes," plausibly "three wires, no markings, left..., yes," but I'll confirm with strict binary questions, and I'll push Blind to speak aloud to Mute directly, since that channel exists and is going unused.

```
speak(text="Round 3 status for both of you: the light is now RED. Full sequence so far: purple, then yellow, then red — it is cycling. Display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: position 1 yellow, position 2 red, position 3 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your last message began with thumbs down, so I understand my guess about your code was wrong. New strict protocol — use ONLY these five signs: a row of fists means that number; thumbs up means yes; thumbs down means no; open hands with both palms means new point; the writing hand means 'the manual says'. Avoid the pointing and palm signs; I cannot decode them. Now answer these questions in order, one sign each, separated by the both-palms sign. One: does the manual cover this bomb type — colour-changing light, display, three wires? Two: does the light colour matter? Three: does the display number matter? Four: must Blind cut a wire? Five: if yes, does the correct wire depend on the light colour, the display, or both? Six: if my whole reading is wrong and fists are not numbers, send only the crossed-fingers sign and I will propose a different code next round.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I received your four signs. My best reading: three — no — left — yes. Confirm with gestures only, thumbs up or thumbs down, in this exact order: one, you feel exactly three wires. Two, the wires carry no markings or bumps you can identify by touch. Three, besides the three wires and the light, you feel no other buttons or panels. Most important: SPEAK ALOUD everything you feel — positions, textures, anything engraved, whether the light feels warm. Mute can hear your voice directly, so your speech reaches the manual-holder without me, even though I will never hear it. Until I relay an explicit instruction from Mute through my voice, cut nothing, press nothing, pull nothing.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👐 👍 👐 👎 👐 👍 👐 👍 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✊ 👐 ✊ 👐 ✊ ✊ 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✊ 👐 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Decoding Mute with the agreed protocol, splitting on 👐: 👍 / 👍 / 👎 / 👍 / 👍 / ✊✊✊ / ✊ / ✊ / ✊✊ / ✊✊✊✊ / ✊✊✊ / ✊✊✊✊✊ / ✊ / 👍👎. Read against my six questions: yes the manual covers it, yes the light matters, no the display doesn't, yes a wire must be cut, yes it depends on the light colour — and no crossed-fingers, so the code itself is confirmed. But the tail of numbers (3-1-1-2-4-3-5-1) is genuinely ambiguous: as colour-index→wire pairs it breaks (wire 4 and 5 don't exist), as a flat list I can't anchor it to colours, and the trailing 👍👎 is unexplained. I will not relay a guess to Blind. The fix is to force an unambiguous format: one wire number per known cycle colour, in an order I dictate, plus a yes/no on whether more than four colours exist. Blind's 👍👍👍 cleanly confirms three wires, no markings, no other parts. Light is green this round — cycle now reads purple, yellow, red, green.

```
speak(text="Round 4 status: the light is GREEN. Confirmed cycle: purple, yellow, red, green. Display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I decoded your answers. Manual covers this bomb: YES. Light colour matters: YES. Display matters: NO. A wire must be cut: YES. It depends on the light colour: YES. My fist code is confirmed since you sent no crossed fingers. But the string of numbers at the end was ambiguous — I cannot tell which number belongs to which colour. Answer in this exact format, and nothing else: for the cycle colours in this order — purple, yellow, red, green — send the wire number to cut for each, as fists, with the both-palms sign between groups. Four groups total. Then one more message: thumbs up if the light cycle has more than four colours, thumbs down if exactly four, and if more than four, add a fifth group of fists for the wire to cut under the fifth colour. Do not re-explain anything else.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: your three thumbs up were received and understood — three wires, no markings, no other parts. Well done. Next: answer thumbs up or down only. One: can you reliably tell the left end from the right end by touch alone — for example an edge, a seam, or the display plate on one side? Two: do the three wires feel different from each other by thickness or texture? Also, keep SPEAKING ALOUD to Mute — describe each wire's texture and position out loud; Mute hears you even though I never will. Mute is preparing the cut instruction; it should arrive through my voice next round. Touch nothing else, cut nothing yet.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👐 👎 👐 👎 👐 👎 👐 👍 👐 👎 👐 ✍ 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✍ 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✊ 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✍ 👐 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ 👐 ✊ 👐 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

The light is now WHITE — a fifth colour, so the cycle is longer than I thought. Sequence so far: purple, yellow, red, green, white. Display still 0, wires unchanged.

Blind's 👍👎 maps cleanly onto my two questions: yes — can tell left from right; no — wires feel alike. That channel works; I'll confirm it and pin down a position convention, because "left" is meaningless unless we anchor it to something Blind can feel, like the display plate.

Mute's message, though, I cannot trust my decode of. Against my requested format — four fist-groups, then a yes/no — Mute sent six thumbs (👎👎👎👎👍👎), then "manual-says" marks mixed with the numbers 7, 3, 1, 4, 5, 1. Wire numbers can only be 1–3, so 4, 5 and 7 cannot mean wires; they might mean colour positions, page numbers, or counts — I can't tell, and I will not relay an ambiguous cutting order to Blind. One pattern tempts me: the lone 👍 sitting in the fifth thumb slot, exactly where white would fall if Mute were walking the cycle saying "cut / don't cut." White happens to be showing right now. But "maybe" detonates bombs. So I'm forcing Mute into a rigid, unambiguous format: one yes/no question about white, and if yes, at most three fists — a number that can only be a wire. Everything else this turn is forbidden. The light cycles, so no information expires; I can afford to spend rounds buying certainty.

```
speak(text="Round 5 status: the light is WHITE. Full cycle observed: purple, yellow, red, green, white. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green, left to right. Mute is being asked for the cutting rule in a strict format; the instruction to you will come only as my spoken words 'CUT WIRE number now'. Until you hear exactly that phrase from me, nothing gets cut, pressed or pulled — even if the light returns to a colour you suspect.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I could not decode your last message reliably. Thumbs I understand; but 4, 5 and 7 fists cannot be wire numbers, so those groups must mean something else and I will not guess with lives at stake. New rule, which overrides everything: I ask ONE question per round. You answer with ONE sign, thumbs up or thumbs down, and only if the answer is thumbs up you may then add between one and three fists — never more, since wires number three. Do not use the writing-hand sign this round. Do not send anything else. This round's question: should Blind cut a wire while the light is WHITE? If yes, add the wire number as fists, using my numbering: 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost when facing the side with the display. If no, send only the thumbs down and nothing after it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: I read your last two signs as: yes, you can tell left from right by touch; no, the wires feel identical to each other. If that reading is wrong send one thumbs down; if right send one thumbs up, and nothing else with it. Second question, one more sign after that: can you find the display plate by touch — the flat panel that shows the number? I am defining positions now: wire 1 means the leftmost wire WHEN FACING the display plate; wire 2 the middle; wire 3 the rightmost. Everything depends on you and Mute and me meaning the same thing by 'wire one'. Status: the light is white this round; the full cycle so far is purple, yellow, red, green, white. Mute's instruction is not decoded yet. You will hear the words CUT WIRE, then a number, then NOW, from my voice only, when it is time. Keep speaking aloud to Mute — tell him what the display plate feels like and which wire is leftmost facing it.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Mute's 👎 is the first fully clean decode: no cut during white — the strict one-question protocol works, so I'll keep it. Blind's 👍👍 answers both my questions: my reading was right and the display plate is findable by touch. Position convention is now safe.

The light is ORANGE this round — a sixth colour. Sequence: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange. Since the colour only lives with me (Blind can't see it, Mute can't see anything) and it changes every round, the urgent question is always about the colour showing right now. So this round: ask Mute about orange. And drill the cut procedure into Blind, because when the moment comes it must be immediate — the light will have moved on by next round.

```
speak(text="Round 6 status: the light is ORANGE — a sixth colour. Full cycle observed so far: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your single thumbs down was received and decoded perfectly — do not cut during white. The strict protocol stays. This round's question: should Blind cut a wire while the light is ORANGE? Answer thumbs down for no and nothing else; or thumbs up followed by one to three fists for the wire number — 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost when facing the display plate. Nothing more after the fists.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: your two thumbs up were decoded — my reading was right and you can find the display plate by touch. Positions are locked: facing the display, wire 1 leftmost, wire 2 middle, wire 3 rightmost. Mute's first rule is in: do NOT cut while the light is white. I am collecting the rule for each colour one at a time; this round's colour is orange. The cut command will come ONLY as my spoken words: CUT WIRE, then a number, then NOW. When you hear NOW, cut immediately and completely — the light changes every round, so there is no time to hesitate or wait for a repeat. If you are unsure at any moment, do not cut. Answer with one sign: thumbs up if you fully understand this procedure, thumbs down if not.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute's 👎: no cutting during orange. Blind's 👍: procedure understood. Two clean rounds in a row — the protocol is now solid, and the light is BLUE, a seventh colour. The full cycle looks like: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue.

One-colour-per-round is too slow: seven colours means seven more questions, each answered a round late. Now that the code has survived two rounds uncorrupted, I can safely request the entire table in a single structured message — seven groups separated by the both-palms sign, one per colour in the order I dictate, each group either a lone thumbs down or thumbs up plus a wire number. The slot position does the mapping, so no ambiguity, and I can verify it: if the group count isn't seven, I reject it. That collapses the remaining rounds to one.

```
speak(text="Round 7 status: the light is BLUE — a seventh colour. The full cycle appears to be, in order: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: orange — do not cut — received and logged. Blind has confirmed the procedure. Your one-sign protocol works, so now we finish it in ONE message. Send me the complete cutting table for all seven colours in a single message, in this exact format: exactly SEVEN groups, separated by the both-palms sign, one group per colour, in this order: group 1 purple, group 2 yellow, group 3 red, group 4 green, group 5 white, group 6 orange, group 7 blue. Each group is either a single thumbs down meaning do not cut during that colour, or thumbs up followed by one to three fists for the wire to cut — 1 leftmost, 2 middle, 3 rightmost facing the display plate. I will count the groups; if I do not count exactly seven, I discard the whole message and we return to one question per round. If the manual's cycle differs from my seven colours in count or order, first send the writing-hand sign, then the groups in the manual's cycle order, and I will match them to the light sequence I observe. Nothing else in the message.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: your thumbs up confirmed you understand the procedure — good. Status: this round's colour is blue; I have now seen seven colours cycling: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue. Rules so far: no cutting during white, no cutting during orange. I have asked Mute for the complete table for every colour at once, in a format I can verify; expect the cut command only as my spoken words CUT WIRE, then a number, then NOW. Until then: hands off, keep speaking aloud anything you feel — Mute may need it. If the light ever stops changing, or the display number ever changes from 0, tell Mute aloud immediately and send me a thumbs down.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👐 👎 👐 👎 👐 👎 👐 👎 👐 👎 👐 👍 ✊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light is back to PURPLE — one full cycle observed and the phase wrapped exactly: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue, purple. Period seven, locked to rounds.

Mute's message decodes perfectly against the requested format: exactly seven groups — 👎, 👎, 👎, 👎, 👎, 👎, 👍✊ — purple no, yellow no, red no, green no, white no, orange no, **blue: cut wire 1**. And it cross-validates: white and orange came back "no cut" here, matching the single-question answers Mute gave in rounds 6 and 7 under a different message structure. Two independent encodings agreeing is what convinces me. So the rule: cut the leftmost wire (yellow) only while the light is blue.

Now the timing problem I have to solve before giving a go order: the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf — I speak last, so anything I say lands a full round late. If I wait until I see blue and then say "cut," Blind hears it during yellow. The command must be sent one round early: I speak during orange, Blind receives and cuts during blue. That only works if the cycle is truly rigid — which two full observations support, but I want Mute's manual to confirm the schedule before betting lives on a prediction. So this turn: confirm the cycle mechanics with Mute, and give Blind the complete rule plus the exact execution plan, including the "command arrives during blue, cut instantly" contract. Blue is six rounds out; there is time to do this properly.

```
speak(text="Round 8 status: the light is back to PURPLE — the cycle has wrapped. Confirmed period: seven colours, purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue, then purple again. Display still 0. Mute has now sent me the complete cutting table and I have decoded it with verification. The rule is in this message for Blind.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: your table arrived and decoded perfectly — seven groups: purple no, yellow no, red no, green no, white no, orange no, blue YES, cut wire 1. Your white and orange answers match what you told me one question at a time, so I trust the whole table. The rule I will arm: cut the LEFTMOST wire, facing the display plate, only while the light is blue. One question this round, thumbs up or thumbs down, nothing else: does the manual state that the light changes colour on a FIXED repeating schedule — the same colours, in the same order, at the same interval, forever? Thumbs up only if the manual guarantees the fixed schedule; thumbs down if it says the timing is anything else — random, accelerating, or dependent on actions. If thumbs down, I will ask what it does say before we arm anything.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind: the complete rule is decoded and cross-verified. Cut ONE wire only: wire 1, the LEFTMOST wire when facing the display plate. Cut it ONLY while the light is BLUE. Every other colour: hands completely off. Now the timing plan, and this part is critical because my voice reaches you one round after I speak. The light cycle is rigid: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue, repeat. When the light is ORANGE, I will speak the words: CUT WIRE 1 NOW. You will hear those words at the very start of the NEXT round — and that next round is the blue round. When you hear CUT WIRE 1 NOW, cut the leftmost wire immediately: no waiting, no second confirmation, the words themselves are the confirmation. Between now and then: locate wire 1 precisely, ready your tool, rehearse the motion without cutting. Two more things to report aloud, one sign for each afterwards. Does the light bulb feel warm or hot against your hand, and hotter for some colours than others? Do you hear or feel any click or hum when the colour changes? Mute's manual may match your answers. Final sign now: thumbs up if you understand the plan, thumbs down if anything is unclear.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👎]

Mute's 👍 seals the last mechanical question: the manual guarantees a fixed repeating schedule, and my own observations agree — round 9 is yellow, exactly where the cycle says it should be. Blind's 👍👎👎 decodes as: plan understood, light gives no perceptible heat, no click at colour change. That last part matters: Blind has no independent clock at all — no light, no sound, no warmth — so my spoken phrase is the *only* trigger that can exist. That makes the command-phrase design load-bearing, and it makes one thing I said earlier wrong: I told Blind to watch the display number, which Blind cannot do. Retracting that now.

The cut cell of Mute's table was format-verified and the white/orange cells were independently confirmed in single-question rounds. With four free rounds before I must spend the orange round sending the command, I'll burn them on per-cell verification, starting with the only cell that kills us if it's wrong: blue.

```
speak(text="Round 9 status: light YELLOW, exactly on schedule — the second lap of the cycle is running as predicted. Display still 0. Mute's manual confirms the schedule is fixed forever.
```
